definitions.explanation: Describes a genuine and wholehearted attitude toward something, especially work, study, or interpersonal relationships. Implies deep commitment and lack of pretense.

examples.japanese: {真摯|しんし}に{受|う}け{止|と}める。
{彼|かれ}は{仕事|しごと}に{真摯|しんし}に{取|と}り{組|く}んでいる。
examples.english: He is earnestly committed to his work.

examples.japanese: {批判|ひはん}を{真摯|しんし}に{受|う}け{止|と}め、{改善|かいぜん}に{努|つと}めます。
examples.english: I will take the criticism seriously and work toward improvement.

notes:
USAGE:
Often used in formal or written contexts, especially in business and official statements. The adverbial form {真摯|しんし}に is extremely common, particularly in the set phrase {真摯|しんし}に{受|う}け{止|と}める (to take something seriously/sincerely).

KANJI:
{真|しん} means "true" and {摯|し} means "earnest." The character {摯|し} is rarely used outside this compound.

COMMON COLLOCATIONS:
- {真摯|しんし}に{受|う}け{止|と}める: to take seriously
- {真摯|しんし}に{取|と}り{組|く}む: to tackle earnestly
- {真摯|しんし}な{態度|たいど}: a sincere attitude
- {真摯|しんし}に{向|む}き{合|あ}う: to face sincerely
